title: Quick look 1: review replay on known gstack bugs
author: GSTA-11
question: Do gstack's reviewer prompts catch known gstack bugs more often than a two-sentence prompt, at what false-alarm rate and cost, split by bugs gstack's review caught and bugs that escaped it? Does gstack bring Haiku 5.5 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to Opus 5.5 at review?

arms.name: plain
arms.description: One call with a two-sentence review prompt and the diff.

arms.name: gstack
arms.description: The reviewers /review dispatches, one call each, rendered from gstack's own text.

tasks.source: public garrytan/gstack history, mined by mine.ts and picked by select.ts: 6 escaped and 6 review-caught defects, 12 decoys

primary.definition: A finding at the defect's file that the judge says names the defect
Any shown CRITICAL finding on a decoy

rules: Every metric is reported for all cases, the escaped stratum and the review-caught stratum.
A unit counts only when every reviewer call returned and every right-file finding has a judge verdict.

approval.source: gate 1 of the v1 plan (first cap $500), moved up at his request

money.reservation: A reserve row at each call's worst case before it is sent, settled with measured usage.
money.stop_rule: A refused reservation stops the run: incomplete, never rerun to change a result.

peg.note: No OpenRouter key at preregistration; the smoke step reads the Data API before the first paid call and records meta.as_of with the results.

limits: Effort is medium in both arms, lighter than gstack runs itself.
Five of six escaped defects come from early gstack; the size match does not match era.
6 escaped and 6 review-caught defects: every comparison is descriptive.
